scope: All three supplied main pages, four figures and the 26-reference bibliography; SI protocols/figures and cited full sources unreviewed.

bibliographic_scope.title: SnSe Nanocrystals: Synthesis, Structure, Optical Properties, and Surface Chemistry
bibliographic_scope.authors: William J. Baumgardner; Joshua J. Choi; Yee-Fun Lim; Tobias Hanrath
bibliographic_scope.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

preparation_details.selenium_stock: 2 mL of 0.1 M trioctylphosphine:selenium is added to 14 mL degassed oleylamine under inert atmosphere; upstream stock formulation and gas identity are absent.
preparation_details.tin_stock: 780 µL of the named tin silylamide is diluted in 6 mL oleylamine and injected; density/moles/final stock volume are not inferred.
preparation_details.temperature_scope: The general interval is 65–175 °C. The main explicitly identifies 155 °C in Figure 1 and 105/175 °C in Figure 2. Other plot positions are not treated as exact tabulated recipe conditions.
preparation_details.ligand_and_quench: 3 mL oleic acid shortly after nucleation; mixture quenched after 2 min. The source does not more precisely define the quench clock or quench technique.
preparation_details.purification: Hexane solvent and isopropanol antisolvent; volume, separation settings, cycles and final state unknown.

structural_scope.155C: Figure 1A/B irregular pseudospherical particles, stacking faults and indexed (200)/(111) fringes; 100 nm and 5 nm scale bars. Exact mean size unreported.
structural_scope.unit_cell_model: Figure 1C shows (001) and (010) projections of a Pnma model. No coordinates, unit-cell parameters or specimen-bound refinement supplied.
structural_scope.XRD: Figure 2A/B primarily Pnma at 175 °C and Cmcm character at 105 °C, subject to explicit resolution uncertainty. Source cites JPCD 32-1382 and 03-065-3876; databases not independently looked up.
structural_scope.d_spacing_series: Figure 2C plots (131) and (200) d spacings versus reaction temperature with literature lines. Exact plotted values/uncertainties and point labels are not tabulated in the main; original graph preserved without invented precision.
structural_scope.size_basis: TEM particle diameter differs from Scherrer grain size; the latter is typically 30–40% smaller.
structural_scope.EDX: Reported Sn:Se 48:52; precise ratio basis and specimen temperature not separately specified.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Figures 1–2 and structural discussion

optical_series.figure3_error_bars: Particle-size distributions within a sample, not uncertainty in its mean.
optical_series.sample_mapping: Main does not provide a one-to-one exact Figure 3 point-to-temperature preparation table.
optical_series.direct_gap: Absorbance/PL comparison referred to unreviewed Figure S3; no exact direct-gap series is invented.
optical_series.lifetime: Decay faster than 5 ns instrumental resolution; no resolved lifetime fit.

literature_context.scope: Background and cited material constants; not per-specimen measured values.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Optical properties and Figure 3

surface_branches.tin_oleate: Crude SnSe QDs reported without reconstructable alternative recipe.
surface_branches.early_oleic_acid: Nucleation inhibited when oleic acid precedes tin injection; control dose and temperature not specified.
surface_branches.timing_series: Final size distribution independent of tested oleic-acid injection time; exact times are in unreviewed Figure S4.
surface_branches.FTIR: As-synthesized NC-film FTIR signatures consistent with oleic-acid passivation; Figure S5 unreviewed.
surface_branches.DDT_exchange: Stable suspension after displacing oleate with dodecanethiol.
surface_branches.DDT_growth: Replacement growth ligand promotes anisotropic elongated/branched structures; Figure S6 unreviewed.
surface_branches.EDT: Readily replaces oleate; treated NCs insoluble in organic/aqueous solvents.
surface_branches.short_acids: Formic, acetic and oxalic acid are cited as immobilizing/improving coupling in prior work. The supplied main provides this study’s formic-acid film test, not separate acetic/oxalic preparation experiments.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3, Surface chemistry discussion

electrical_scope.formic_film: Interdigitated gold electrodes covered by formic-acid-passivated SnSe NC film; deposition and thickness unreported. The relative order of ligand treatment and film deposition, and the initial ligand surface, are not given.
electrical_scope.oleate_control: Similar effects referenced in Figure S7, not supplied/read.
electrical_scope.CV: Oleic-acid-capped SnSe, Ag/Ag+ reference. Electrolyte, solvent, concentration, scan rate and exact numerical HOMO/LUMO values not stated; no values digitized.
electrical_scope.batch_linkage: Figure 4A/B formic film and Figure 4C/D oleate electrochemistry are not merged into an assumed single batch.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 4 caption and discussion

SI_inventory.note: Names derived from main references only; no SI reading claimed.

source_interpretation.topic: Ligand addition controls nucleation and growth
source_interpretation.text: Oleic acid before tin injection inhibits nucleation. The authors attribute this to strong tin-oleate binding, which lowers the nucleation driving force. Introducing oleic acid after precursor mixing accelerates growth toward an equilibrium size. They report that the final size distribution was independent of the ligand-injection time in their tested series; exact times and Figure S4 remain outside this main-only scope.

The 175 °C and 105 °C XRD patterns are described as primarily Pnma and Cmcm, respectively. The same discussion warns that peak broadening and similar structures prevent an unambiguous assignment. Figure 1c is a Pnma reference model, not a measured atom-coordinate dataset or proof of a unique 155 °C phase.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Figures 1–2 and phase discussion

source_interpretation.topic: Particle size is not crystallite size
source_interpretation.text: TEM shows irregular pseudospherical particles and HRTEM shows stacking faults. The authors report that Scherrer grain sizes are typically 30–40% smaller than TEM particle diameters. Figure 3 error bars represent within-sample size distributions, not uncertainty in sample means. Neither the size-series points nor optical gaps are assigned here to an unstated recipe temperature.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2, TEM, Scherrer comparison and Figure 3

source_interpretation.text: Dodecanethiol displaces oleate and yields a stable suspension; its use during synthesis promotes elongated and branched structures. Ethanedithiol treatment instead immobilizes/crosslinks the NCs, making them insoluble in organic and aqueous solvents. These different operations remain separate; dose, exact conditions and referenced SI images are unavailable in this main-only scope.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3, Ligand-exchange and modified-growth discussion

source_interpretation.text: Formic-acid-passivated films are photoconductive but show hysteresis and photocurrent degradation. The authors use the energy alignment inferred from cyclic voltammetry to argue that photo-oxidation of surface-bound carboxylic acids likely contributes. This is a source-attributed explanation, not a measured reaction yield or proof that every current change has that origin.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 4 and transport interpretation

source_interpretation.topic: Optical confinement has a series-level scope
source_interpretation.text: The source reports 4–10 nm particles and indirect gaps from 0.9 to approximately 1.3 eV, with confinement tapering near 10 nm. Weak emission and a decay faster than the 5 ns instrument response do not establish a resolved fluorescence lifetime or quantum yield. Bulk reference gaps and dielectric constants are literature comparisons rather than measured properties of each prepared sample.

claims.label: Resolution limit
claims.statement: Peak broadening and close structural similarity prevent conclusive unambiguous phase assignment.

source_conflicts.handling: Retain the author labels and explicit uncertainty together; no phase fractions or unique atom coordinates are inferred.
